draft.title: Ethical dilemmas in literature
card: An ethical dilemma is a situation where a character must choose between options and each choice has a cost. No choice is clearly right.
Dilemmas usually set two values against each other, such as loyalty and honesty, or duty and mercy. Choosing one value means giving up part of the other.
Writers use dilemmas to invite readers to weigh the values for themselves. The reader asks what the character gains and loses, and what they would do.
A strong reading explains the competing values and points to evidence from the text. It does not just declare the character good or bad.
draft.remember: A dilemma sets values against each other, and readers weigh them using evidence.

a.q: In a novel, Priya sees her best friend cheat in an exam. Telling the teacher is honest but betrays her friend. Why is this an ethical dilemma?
opts: Each choice upholds one value and costs another
Priya is clearly wrong whichever way she acts
The friend is a villain and Priya is a hero
Priya has only one possible choice to make
a.why: Honesty and loyalty pull in opposite directions, so every option has a cost and none is clearly right. It is not a case of a simple wrong choice, because the text sets up real values on both sides.
a.clue: Look for the two values that pull against each other.

b.q: A short story shows Tom, a ferry captain, who can save a few passengers quickly or search longer for many, at the risk of losing all. What is the best way for a reader to respond?
opts: Weigh the values at stake and use evidence from the text
Decide which choice is right and ignore the other
Treat Tom as a villain because someone is harmed
Assume the writer wants readers to feel no doubt
b.why: A dilemma invites readers to weigh competing values, such as mercy and duty, using evidence from the text. Declaring Tom good or bad skips the weighing, which is the tempting mistake because harm occurs either way.
b.clue: No easy right answer means the reasoning matters most.

a.best: Each choice upholds one value and costs another

b.best: Weigh the values at stake and use evidence from the text
